_comment: Validate->fix loop. Wraps L1 (basic_checks) + L2 (validator) + modifier so Claude can iteratively repair a schematic until it passes. Every threshold/limit/severity gate lives here, never in fixer.py.

loop._comment: Maximum repair attempts. Each iteration: validate -> ask Claude for ops -> apply -> re-validate. Stops early on PASS or when no progress is made (issue count does not drop two iterations in a row).

gates._comment: Which severities the loop tries to fix and which block declaring success. fix_severities = sent to Claude; success_blocking_severities = if any remain after the loop, status=FAIL. Lowering thresholds here makes the loop stricter without code changes.

claude._comment: Which model to ask for repairs and what shape we expect back. The prompt template lives in fixer.py because it weaves runtime data; the controllable knobs are here.
claude._model_null_comment: null = use the default deep model from .env (CLAUDE_MODEL_DEEP).

safety._comment: What the loop refuses to do without explicit opt-in. delete_components stays off by default because deleting a part the user placed is rarely the right repair for a missing-decoupling-cap or wrong-value issue.

layout_guidance._comment: Distance hints injected into the fixer prompt. Editing these tunes Claude's placement choices without touching Python. mm units. rail_port_mm matches conventions.json:wire.long_threshold_mm by intent — if you change one, change the other.
